title: Vertex DataHub - peering & private endpoints discovery
summary: Introductory discovery focused on private deployment networking: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, cross-account routing, region constraints and IP overlap concerns. SE dug into connectivity checks, required configs (route tables, SGs, NACLs), and KMS/SAML integration points. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share network checklist & architecture diagram, customer to validate CIDR allocations and schedule pilot week-of-07-21.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Private Service Connect
Cross-account peering and Transit Gateway considerations
Private endpoints, NLB vs ALB for TLS termination
Audit logs, SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
action_items: Priya Kapoor - send Redwood private deployment network checklist + sample VPC diagram - 2025-07-11

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-09 15:00 PDT | Duration 48 min | Attendees: Liam Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Vertex Infra), Sasha Gupta (Vertex Security), Evan Ortiz (Platform)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Liam, AE on the Redwood side.
[00:12] Mark: Mark here, infra lead at Vertex DataHub. We're looking at private deployments — basically want the runtime inside our AWS org, private endpoints, no public egress.
[00:23] Priya: Hi all, Priya from Redwood SE. I'll run through the technical checklist in a bit. Just to confirm: you're on AWS, single account or multi-account?
[00:30] Mark: Multi-account right now. We have separate prod and infra accounts, then a security account. So cross-account peering is a requirement — we don't want a public endpoint.
[00:42] Sasha: From security, we need KMS integration, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and the ability to restrict egress to our proxy. Also region constraint: primary in us-east-1, backup in eu-west-1.
[00:55] Priya: Got it. Common pattern we see is two options: classic VPC peering or using PrivateLink / AWS PrivateLink with interface endpoints. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:12] Evan: Can you clarify the tradeoffs again? I'm particularly worried about CIDR overlap — we have some old /16s floating around.
[01:20] Priya: Sure. VPC peering is simplest network-wise but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table updates. PrivateLink avoids that by exposing an interface endpoint in consumer VPCs — but that means ENIs in the consumer, some additional configuration, and slightly different failover semantics. Also PrivateLink carries cross-account endpoint permissions.
[01:39] Mark: What about Transit Gateway? We use TGW for a lot of inter-VPC traffic. Could Redwood live behind that?
[01:46] Priya: Yes, Redwood private deployment can be connected via TGW. We typically ask for routing rules to allow specific prefix lists. Few gotchas: ensure propagation to the right route tables and that the TGW attachments include the subnet ranges we expect.
[02:00] Liam: From product side, we support private control plane with customer-managed networking. So you can keep control of ingress/egress, and we support peering or interface endpoints.
[02:12] Sasha: About egress: we require all egress to go through our HTTP proxy and be logged. Can Redwood agents be configured to use a customer proxy or forced via NAT?
[02:21] Priya: Yes, there are two approaches — configure the hosts to use your proxy or lock egress via route/NAT gateway. For strict environments we recommend forcing egress through the proxy/NAT and ensuring security groups only allow outbound to that proxy's IPs.
[02:36] Mark: What's the startup IP footprint? How many ENIs, public IPs, etc should we plan?
[02:41] Priya: For a small pilot (3-node cluster) expect about 3-6 ENIs for control plane plus worker ENIs for the runtime. We'll send a sizing doc but plan for /24 per subnet to be safe.
[02:57] Speaker 4: (mumble) also curious about load balancer, TLS termination.
[03:02] Priya: Good point. Most customers front Redwood with an NLB for TCP and TLS passthrough or an NLB+ALB combo if you want Layer 7 routing. For certs you can terminate at your LB or pass through — both supported. If you need private CA integration, we can accept certs via our deployment package.
[03:22] Sasha: Our security policy requires keys to be customer-managed, ideally in KMS with key policies scoped to the resource. Can Redwood use our KMS keys?
[03:30] Priya: Yes, we support CMKs. We'll need an IAM role that Redwood components can assume and kms:Decrypt permissions scoped to the key. We'll document the exact permissions.
[03:42] Mark: Any constraints on region pairing? For example, a private deployment in us-east-1 and backup in eu-west-1 — anything special we should know?
[03:51] Priya: Multi-region is supported, but keep in mind cross-region latency for KV cache warmup and model weights synchronization. We recommend model-version pinning and a regional failover strategy. Also some instance types and AMI images differ by region — we can provide a supported region matrix.
[04:10] Liam: Quick commercial note — Dedicated/reserved capacity is different from Private deployment pricing. For private, there is a platform license plus infra. We'll send a rough pricing sketch after the checklist.
[04:21] Evan: On the network ACLs and security groups, do you need inbound from all our subnets or only specific ones?
[04:28] Priya: Only specific CIDR prefixes that you want to allow. We'll ask for a prefix list of allowed consumer subnets. It's best to lock SGs down to exact ports (usually 443 and a few management ports) and the IPs of your attach points.
[04:43] Mark: What about IP overlap? We have a few legacy networks, could that block peering?
[04:49] Priya: Yes, overlap prevents VPC peering. That's where PrivateLink helps. Alternatively, you can set up NAT-based routing or a peering proxy but that's more work. If you run into overlap we can discuss a MIGRATION plan or using interface endpoints.
[05:05] Sasha: Audit logs — we need all control plane logs forwarded for compliance, ideally to a Kinesis or S3 destination in our account. Can Redwood ship logs to our S3 bucket?
[05:15] Priya: We support log forwarding to customer S3/Kinesis/Kafka with cross-account permissions. We'll include an example policy in the checklist.
[05:24] Mark: Is there an option for an air-gapped install or on-prem?
[05:29] Priya: We do offer an on-prem package for highly regulated customers, but that has a different install process and longer lead time. It can be completely air-gapped if needed.
[05:38] Speaker 4: (overlap) what's the recommended way to handle updates — rolling vs blue-green?
[05:43] Priya: For private installs we support canary and rolling rollouts. We have tooling for model version pinning and automatic fallback to a previous model if regressions are detected.
[05:55] Liam: Let's dig into the pilot. Suggested scope: small dev VPC peering or interface endpoint, test requests to inference endpoints, measure latency and authentication flows, and validate KMS and SSO. Does that align?
[06:07] Mark: Yes. Success criteria: sub-50ms median token latency for our short-form prompts and no public egress from the infra account. Also KMS keys used for secrets and SAML for access controls.
[06:20] Priya: We'll help design the test prompts and the eval harness. We'll also provide a minimal VPC template.
[06:26] Sasha: About SAML and RBAC mapping — our identity provider is Okta. We need role mapping so our engineers can assume roles with scoped permissions, not full admin.
[06:35] Priya: Okta is supported. We'll document the SAML assertion attributes we expect and how to map them to Redwood roles.
[06:43] Evan: Regarding firewall egress: we run a corporate proxy that does TLS interception. Any issues with the inference traffic?
[06:50] Priya: If the proxy terminates TLS you'll need to install our certs or configure the agent to trust your proxy cert. If you force egress through the proxy, ensure outbound to your model registry endpoints is allowed.
[07:04] Mark: How are models stored? Do you host weights or are they pulled from S3 in our account?
[07:10] Priya: For private, models can either be hosted by Redwood in a private S3 we manage or pulled from your S3 via role-based access. Many customers prefer pulling from their own S3 bucket so they retain data control.
[07:21] Speaker 4: (murmur) and quantization?
[07:24] Priya: We support quantized builds to reduce memory and cost. If you need to keep weights in your account we can accept quantized artifacts as part of the deployment.
[07:33] Liam: A few operational questions we often get: patching cadence, incident response, and RTO/RPO commitments for the private model.
[07:40] Priya: We publish our patching windows; for private installs we align patching with your maintenance windows. Incident response: Redwood can provide runbooks and a pager rotation as an add-on. RTO/RPO will be part of the SLA in an enterprise contract.
[07:54] Sasha: On compliance docs — can you share SOC2 type 2 report and penetration test summary?
[07:59] Liam: Yes, we'll share SOC2 docs and a redacted pen test. We'll drop them in the follow-up email.
[08:06] Mark: Are there any ports besides 443 we should expect?
[08:10] Priya: Mostly 443 for inference API. Management and telemetry use a few additional ports; we'll list them explicitly.
[08:17] Evan: For cross-account role assumption, do you have templates for the trust policy?
[08:21] Priya: Yes, included in the checklist. We'll also provide example IAM policies with least privilege.
[08:28] Speaker 4: (interrupt) latency SLO — how do you measure?
[08:32] Priya: We instrument token-level latency and request-level latency; for the pilot we'll provide dashboards and token-level traces so you can correlate with your own telemetry.
[08:40] Liam: Anything else on networking we should cover?
[08:43] Mark: Two final things — VPN vs Direct Connect, and data egress costs. We use Direct Connect for our main colo, does Redwood support connecting over DX?
[08:52] Priya: Direct Connect is supported; you'll treat the deployment as any other VPC attachment. Regarding egress costs, if the model weights are hosted in your account that reduces cross-account egress. We'll include cost guidance in the pricing sketch.
[09:05] Sasha: Also need to confirm data residency — logs and metrics for EU customers must stay in EU regions.
[09:11] Priya: We can scope logging to a region and keep backups there. We'll highlight data residency controls in the doc.
[09:19] Liam: Great — recap quick: Redwood sends checklist, diagrams, IAM/KMS examples, SOC2 docs; Vertex validates CIDRs and schedules pilot.
[09:28] Mark: Sounds good. Any blockers today?
[09:31] Evan: Not from infra; security will verify KMS policies.
[09:34] Sasha: We'll need the sample policies to review.
[09:36] Priya: We'll include them.
[09:40] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a single email containing attachments and proposed pilot dates.
[09:45] Mark: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "peer-ing" spelled variably).
